newsitem.title: UK: JCI confident of Lonrho deal.
newsitem.headline: JCI confident of Lonrho deal.

text.p: The chairman of JCI Ltd is confident that a deal can be reached for a merger with Lonrho PLC which could create one of the world's largest mining companies, the Financial Times said on Thursday.
Mzi Khumalo, chairman of South Africa's first black-controlled mining firm, said he was optimistic about a deal soon.
"JCI wants a broad agreement pretty soon. After that, we can handle the detailed, technical work," he said before flying back to South Africa on Wednesday.
Khumalo, who made the initial approach to the conglomerate, added that he would return to London on Monday for what he hoped would be final talks.

"When it became clear that the European Union would not allow Anglo American to maintain its 27 percent take in Lonrho, I knew it was open season and that JCI had to make its move," he told the newspaper.
JCI and Lonrho admitted on Monday that they were in talks on a possible merger which could create a mining company with market capitalisation of more than $3 billion.
But Business Day newspaper in Johannessburg reported on Monday that Avmin Ltd and Gencor Ltd were also interested in tying up with Lonrho.
Last month the European Commission forced Anglo American of South Africa Ltd to cut its 27.5 percent stake in Lonrho to 9.99 percent over the next two years.
The Commission said Anglo platinum interests combined with that of Lonrho would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo and Gencor.
